name: Adamant - North Ridge via Variation of Kaufman Route
text: [overview] Ascend the Turret glacier to a point above the gully-ramp of that route, cross the bergshrund to easy ice, then follow the rock edge to a larger ramp.
[overview] A friction-slab crack at 5.5 reaches a sheltered belay, then snow and ice, then a walk to the summit.
[approach] From the Fairy Meadow hut, ascend the Granite Glacier until you reach the Turret Glacier.
[approach] Where crevasses and icefalls allow, step onto the Turret Glacier on either flank of the nunatak, then keep to its left side along the base of Adamant's north ridge.
[approach] The Kaufman route leaves to the left beneath a prominent triangular snow patch;

[descent_text] The other option is to go west from the summit to the Adamant-Turret col (easy fifth class or a short rappel) and rappel the steep ice and snow over the bergshrund onto the upper Turret Glacier.
[descent_text] That glacier is steep and heavily crevassed, so it is not the casual way down.

name: Adamant-Turret-Austerity Traverse
text: [overview] Go up the left part of the Turret Glacier until Adamant's North Ridge can be reached, then follow its crest to the summit (Class 3 and 4 dominate, with some easy Class 5).
[overview] the snow arete leads to Turret's summit.
[overview] Return to the Granite glacier by Austerity's standard route.
[approach] From the Fairy Meadow hut, go up the moraine to the Granite Glacier and then up the left side of the Turret Glacier until you can step onto the north ridge of Adamant.
[descent_text] The traverse finishes by going down the Austerity standard route to the Granite Glacier.

[descent_text] From the col, the steep snow and ice slope can be downclimbed or rappelled, and the bergshrund below it has to be crossed from above without a chance to scout it, so someone in the party should know the way.
[descent_text] Beyond it, follow the upper Granite Glacier down through the crevasses toward Fairy Meadow.

name: Austerity - Std Route
text: [approach] Leave Fairy Meadow on the path over the moraine to the Granite Glacier, then cross the fairly flat but crevassed glacier beneath Pioneer and Adamant.
[approach] Pass below the lower northeast ridge of Austerity and, somewhere under its northwest ridge, thread through the crevasses into the basin between that ridge and the north ridge of Ironman.

[descent_text] From the col, the steep snow and ice slope can be downclimbed or rappelled, and the bergshrund below it has to be crossed from above without a chance to scout it, so someone in the party should know the way.
[descent_text] Beyond it, follow the upper Granite Glacier down through the crevasses toward Fairy Meadow.

name: Gog East Face
text: [approach] From the Fairy Meadow hut, follow the path toward Friendship Col and the Echo Glacier.
[approach] Gog is the higher, closer-to-the-col summit of the Gog-Magog pair, and the route starts on its east face, reached by hiking across the snow below it and crossing the moat to the rock.
[descent_text] Cross the moat and walk down the snowfield toward the Friendship Col trail and the hut.

name: Horn - SE Face and Unicorn
text: [overview] Go from Fairy Meadow up the moraine and Granite glacier to the saddle between Horn and Unicorn, swinging right onto loose class 3 rock.
[approach] From Fairy Meadow, go up the moraine and onto the Granite Glacier toward the Horn-Unicorn col.
[descent_text] From the col, retrace the approach to the Granite Glacier.

name: Magog
text: [approach] From the Fairy Meadow hut, follow the path toward Friendship Col and the Echo Glacier.
[approach] Hike across the snowfield to the east face and cross the moat to rock below the notch between the two summits.
[descent_text] Cross the moat and walk back down the snowfield toward the hut.

name: Mount Quadrant West Face to North Summit (Stem-winder)
text: [overview] Snow may cover the approach and return.

[approach] From the Fairy Meadow hut, follow the Friendship Col trail until it turns up the snow slopes toward Gog and Magog, then continue straight over the ridge, drop down and around the left side of the lake, and climb back up to the base of Quadrant's north face.
[approach] There is some snow on the approach.

name: Mt Austerity - East Face
text: [approach] From the Fairy Meadow hut, go onto the Granite Glacier and follow it to the Turret Glacier.
[approach] The Turret Glacier is heavily crevassed and needs careful route-finding;
[approach] a high camp on the Granite Glacier cuts the effort.
[approach] The east face is reached from the upper Turret Glacier, where avalanches coming off the face above are a concern.

[descent_text] The usual way down is a variant of the standard route: from the summit, descend toward the Austerity-Ironman col and rappel to the upper Granite Glacier at a spot somewhat east of the col.
[descent_text] Once on the upper Granite Glacier, follow it down through the crevasses toward Fairy Meadow.

name: North Peak of Colossal via East Couloir
text: [overview] Besides rock, expect glacier travel and steep snow.

[overview] Leave Fairy Meadow for the Granite Glacier (its lower part), cross west under the icefall, then work up glacier and snow, staying right of Colossal's east ridge, to the flat basin under the Colossal-Enterprise col.
[overview] Go left up the slope toward the East face couloir, cross the bergshrund, and finish on easy rock and snow.

[overview] To descend, scramble down rock to the saddle separating the north peak from the main summit, head east, facing Fairy Meadow, across a bergshrund via rock and snow, and follow the crest back to the Granite Glacier.
[detailed_rack] Standard glacier-travel kit;
[approach] From Fairy Meadow, cross onto the lower Granite Glacier and move west below the icefall, then gain height on glacier and snow to the right of Colossal's east ridge.
[descent_text] Scramble down rock to the saddle separating the main summit from the north peak, then drop east, toward Fairy Meadow, on rock and snow.
[descent_text] Cross a bergshrund and walk the crest of the east ridge down to the Granite Glacier, then return to the hut.

name: NorthEast Ridge Mt. Austerity (Nester Ridge)
text: [approach] From Fairy Meadow, climb into the upper Granite Glacier and then into the glacial amphitheater between the northeast and northwest ridges of Austerity's north ridge.
[approach] The route starts by crossing the bergshrund a few rope lengths left of the snow and ice gully that gives access to the ridge.
[descent_text] Downclimb the Austerity standard route to the Austerity-Ironman col, an excellent bivouac site, then continue down the standard route onto the upper Granite Glacier.

[descent_text] Broken low-angle rock along the ridge is mostly downclimbed, and the steep snow and ice slope below the col can be rappelled or downclimbed before the bergshrund and the crevasses of the glacier.

name: NW Ridge Quadrant with Rabbit Ears Arete (s)
text: [approach] From the Fairy Meadow hut, head up toward the lower Echo Glacier and pass below the small lakes on it to reach the notch on the northwest ridge of Quadrant.

name: Pioneer via Pioneer Pass & East Ridge
text: [overview] Mixes ice and rock, making it livelier than the usual snowy plod via Friendship Col.
[overview] Get across the bergschrund and climb a high-angle slope of snow or ice to reach the pass.
[overview] Turn right to the rock east ridge, following it to a snow summit and then the rock summit.

[overview] For the descent, follow the usual line down to the col shared by Pioneer and Gothics' eastern summit (a quick party may add that summit), then the glacier, which returns to Fairy Meadow past Friendship Col.
[approach] From Fairy Meadow, hike toward the Adamant-Austerity glacier, but bear left once past the lower end of Sentinel's north ridge.
[approach] Cross the bergshrund and climb the high-angle snow or ice to the pass;
[descent_text] From that col, follow the glacier back to Friendship Col and then down to Fairy Meadow.

name: Sentenel Peak - Shoofly Arete of North Ridge
text: [overview] Starts on the lower Shoestring glacier and heads for the Sentinelle, the peak capping the north end of the North Ridge, with its pair of gunsite notches.
[approach] The line begins on the lowest reaches of the Shoestring Glacier, almost opposite Quadrant's south face, and gains the northern end of Sentinel's north ridge.

name: East Peak of Gothics - "North East" Ridge
text: [overview] From Fairy Meadow go through Friendship Col onto the Gothics Glacier, bear right past Sentinel's south ridge to the col between East Peak and Pioneer, then ascend the steep (usually) snow along the ridge running north-northeast until a conspicuous step of rock
[approach] From the Fairy Meadow base camp take the usual path through Friendship Col onto the glacier.
[approach] Bear right past Sentinel's south ridge, to the col between East Peak and Pioneer, then climb the steep snow slope up the north-northeast ridge to the first prominent rock step.

name: Gibraltar North Face
text: [approach] Gibraltar rises along the glacier's southern margin.
[approach] From the Fairy Meadow base camp take the usual path through Friendship Col onto the glacier.
[approach] The route starts at the obvious splitter hand crack, reached by stepping across the moat from a snow bank;
[approach] check the moat edge before stepping, since the snow there can be undercut.

name: Iron Man- Gibson/Rohn
peak: South & West Faces (from Adamant or AusterityGlacier)
text: [overview] Eight to ten lengthy crack and face pitches on the glacier side of the buttress.
[overview] The original start is now hard to reach after the glacier shrank.
[what_to_bring] ice axe and crampons — the descent drops onto steep late-summer glacier ice;
[what_to_bring] axe alone in good snow
[approach] Ironman is the conspicuous buttress closing the upper Austerity Glacier.
[approach] Access to the Adamants is usually by helicopter, or on foot from Fairy Meadow over Friendship Col and Thor Pass to the Adamant Glacier.
[descent_text] Walk north to the end of the plateau and go down westward by a loose gully system onto the upper Austerity Glacier, starting from fixed slings.
[descent_text] An ice axe and crampons are strongly recommended, because the gully drops onto the steep upper headwall of the glacier.

name: South Buttress, Adamant Mountain
peak: South & West Faces (from Adamant or AusterityGlacier)
text: [overview] A classic south-facing line in the cirque beside the Austerity Glacier.
[overview] A couple of chimney pitches follow, then 200-300 ft of short-roped ground, then a trio of fine pitches and scrambling up to the summit snowfield.
[detailed_rack] A standard rack, with an ice axe and crampons of light weight.
[approach] Access to the Adamants is usually by helicopter, or on foot from Fairy Meadow over Friendship Col and Thor Pass to the Adamant Glacier.
[approach] From the Austerity Glacier reach the col between Adamant and Blackfriars, then head directly up the South Buttress.
[descent_text] The route ends at a summit snowfield, from which the summit of Adamant is a short way on.
[descent_text] Rappel the route, since fixed tat marks every belay, or hike down from the summit on its west side and circle back to the Austerity Glacier.

name: West Buttress of the Horn
peak: South & West Faces (from Adamant or AusterityGlacier)
text: [approach] Access to the Adamants is usually by helicopter, or on foot from Fairy Meadow over Friendship Col and Thor Pass to the Adamant Glacier.

[descent_text] Descend east with short rappels, or from a camp in the Horn and Unicorn basin traverse north over the Unicorn and along the divide separating the Horn basin from the Granite Glacier basin to the saddle, then descend west to the low point of a snowfield above a

name: Glacier Ice Climbs - Everywhere is a route!
Another Fine Day in The Bugaboos
text: [overview] After a short moat pitch, pitches 1 to 3 (5.7) trend through cracks and corners beside a gendarme.
[approach] Cross snow and scree beneath the east buttress of Brenta Spire toward its northeast spur;
[approach] the route begins from the snow in a moat at the foot of that spur.
[descent_text] a short scramble and a final rappel lead into a moat, so an ice axe is useful.

name: Divine Intervention
text: [approach] The east face is reached by the Crescent Glacier.
[approach] From the Kain hut, walk toward the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col but leave that route short of the col, exactly as for Crescent Spire;

name: East Ridge
text: [description] Clean Purcell granite with a well-known gendarme pitch high on the ridge, reached from the Applebee camp above the Bugaboo Glacier.

name: Kain Route (South Ridge)
text: [overview] The south ridge of Bugaboo Spire, approached via moraine and snowfield to the col with Snowpatch, then along the south arete.
[detailed_rack] carry an ice axe, and crampons are possible.
[approach] From the Kain hut or the Applebee campground, follow the north lateral moraine of the Bugaboo Glacier, then cross the snowfield up to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col.
[approach] carry an ice axe and possibly crampons for the snow below the col.

name: Northwest Face
text: [overview] Steep upper snowslopes are threatened by cornices in spring and late in the season.
[detailed_rack] One or two pickets and some slings may help.
[approach] The upper snow can be corniced in late season;

name: Seppuku
text: [overview] wet in early season from snowmelt.
[approach] Follow the Sky Pilot approach to the Stadium Glacier and traverse west toward Copilot.

name: West Ridge
text: [approach] Follow the normal Sky Pilot approach up to the Stadium Glacier, then cross easy snow slopes west to the foot of Copilot.
[approach] Leave the snow and scramble up to the start of a corner, which is where the climbing begins;

name: Energy Crisis
text: [approach] Pass the first lake on its west side and the second on its east side, then continue straight north up the Crescent Glacier to the south face of the spire.
[approach] Parties staying at the Kain hut instead head toward the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col and turn right before reaching it to join the same glacier.

[approach] Parties staying at the Kain hut instead head toward the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col and turn right before reaching it to join the same glacier.
[approach] The route starts off the same large ledge as Paddle Flake, a short scramble above the glacier, but a bit farther right, from a big boulder below a set of flakes.

[approach] Parties staying at the Kain hut instead head toward the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col and turn right before reaching it to join the same glacier.
[approach] Scramble up from the glacier onto the large ledge that the McTech Arete route also starts from, and follow it left past that route to the start.

[approach] Scramble up from the glacier onto a large ledge and follow it left to the start, which is left of McTech Arete and just left of a big left-facing dihedral.

name: Ears Between
text: [approach] From the Applebee Dome camp, go left and up from the campground and head for the foot of the wall, following faint paths through boulders and past what is left of the Crescent Glacier.

name: Crater Couloir, Winter
text: [overview] At most, expect exposed snow slopes to about 50 degrees and possibly some AI2 pitches.
[detailed_rack] Short screws, pickets and two ice tools.

name: Dehydrated on Dalwhinnie
text: [approach] From the hut, cross the Dione Glacier to the foot of the south face.

name: Drilling Dionysus
text: [approach] From the hut, cross the Dione Glacier to the base of the peak.

name: Sunny Chibas
text: [overview] A variation beside the Mags 99 line on Dione's west side, approached by a snow couloir.
[detailed_rack] Crampons, axe, and perhaps tat to replace the first rappel anchor.
[approach] Reach the south face of Dione from the hut by crossing the glacier.
[approach] At the south face, drop well down to an obvious col on your right, pass through it, descend snow then ascend again to the foot of the steep snow couloir serving several west-face lines.
[descent_text] From just south of the summit, rappel the normal route down the east side from fixed cord to bolted rap stations, onto the snowfield capping Petite Dione.

name: SW Buttress of Dione
text: [detailed_rack] add an ice axe, lightweight crampons and, seasonally, snow pickets.
[approach] From the hut, go to Red Tit Col, then follow the broad Dione Glacier across the west flank under the peak's extended south ridge.
[approach] Crossing the moat to reach the rock can be hard in mid to late season.

name: SW Spur
text: [approach] From the hut, cross the Dione Glacier to the foot of the south face.

name: Eternal Darkness
text: [overview] Descent: four 60 m rappels, starting slightly skiers left of the summit, reach a snow and dirt gully;
[descent_text] Further rappels lead into the snow and dirt gully, which can be walked down and circled back under the face to the start.

name: Phillips Ridge Route
text: [beta] Cross to Moraine Lake, climb the south and southeast scree slopes toward the north end of the summit ridge, and ascend the steep couloir (roughly 55 degrees in places, with a narrow line beside the snow).
[hazards] Steep snow couloir with a no-fall runout.
[gear] Ice axe.
[gear] Crampons.
[turnaround] Turn back if the couloir snow is not firm or if rockfall is active above you;
[pitch_detail] Steep snow in a couloir, then about 50 m of scrambling on loose basalt..
[pro_tips] Carry an ice axe and crampons in early season.

name: Back From the Storm
text: [overview] Leftmost line on the Lyell Wall, and among the longest in Icefall Brook.
[approach] The cirque is reached by helicopter, snowmobile or skis from the Bush River road.

name: L'etonnement
text: [overview] Tucked beneath an enormous overlap of rock and unseen until directly below, it holds some of the finest ice of the whole Icefall Brook area.
[approach] Rappel into a deep gully, leaving a fixed line to climb out, then go up steep snow to a bolt, across to another, and up to the base.

name: Ionia NE Spur
text: [overview] Start by crossing from snow onto rock, then work leftward and upward beneath a snow patch to a tooth on the ridgeline;
[approach] Approach through the Tantalus Range to the Lycia and Serratus col, and cross it to the Ionia Glacier.
[approach] Cross the ice to the foot of the Ionia buttress, at its far right edge where the snow meets rock.

name: NW Face
text: [overview] A snow line of steep angle on Lesser Wedge Mountain, holding a sustained 50 degrees from the glacier all the way up, for roughly 100 m of gain.
[detailed_rack] Nobody is known to have placed protection here, though snow pickets would be an option.

name: North Face
text: [overview] A good option if the North Ridge is crowded or snowy, with some May ascents finding good conditions.

name: North Ridge
text: [overview] haul packs down the 5.0 headwall instead of using the steep snow gully, and note the lower traverse is exposed, so a fall while roped could be dangerous.
[overview] Once away from the Hind Hut, traverse moraines to the ridge, go around the lowest cliff band on snow, and take debris-covered slabs to the red band.
[overview] a short rib then gains the summit ridge, where trapdoor cornices have killed climbers.

[approach] From the hut, cross the moraines to the foot of the north ridge and follow the easy lower crest, staying right of the snow, along the easy lower part of the ridge, then work left across snow to get around the lowest cliff band.
[descent_text] Trapdoor cornices on the summit ridge have claimed lives, so stay back from the edge.

name: Gnomon Direct
text: [approach] The approach is short but steep, and an ice axe, sometimes crampons, are needed on the snow early in the season.

[descent_text] From the notch you can escape down the couloir behind it, using a mix of rappels and down-climbing on steep snow and ice, or climb one more long, easier pitch to the rim of the summit plateau and descend from there to the left (north) into the major couloir be
[descent_text] An ice axe and crampons are almost always needed, and anchors may need backing up or replacing, so carry rappel webbing and a few pitons.

name: Keep your Heid
text: [overview] After the summit, descend across the plateau to the descent glacier.
[approach] The approach is short but steep, and an ice axe, sometimes crampons, are needed on the snow early in the season.
[descent_text] From there the plateau leads to the descent glacier;
[descent_text] Carry an ice axe and crampons.

name: Kiss of Death (Sinnes Couloir)
text: [detailed_rack] Conditions are steep snow or neve, with no ice.
[approach] The approach is short but steep, and an ice axe, sometimes crampons, are needed on the snow early in the season.
